definition: Artificially generated data, often produced by another model or simulation, used to supplement or substitute for real-world training data.
details: Synthetic data is increasingly used to train and fine-tune LLMs, particularly for tasks where high-quality real data is scarce, expensive to collect, or raises privacy concerns.
story: Imagine a chef tasting every ingredient before it goes into the pot, deciding what belongs and what would ruin the broth. Think of it this way: Artificially generated data, often produced by another model or simulation, used to supplement or substitute for real-world training data. And here is the clever part: Synthetic data is increasingly used to train and fine-tune LLMs, particularly for tasks where high-quality real data is scarce, expensive to collect, or raises privacy concerns. It is the raw material; the model is only ever as good as what it was fed. And that is Synthetic Data — the unglamorous work everything else stands on.
